newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bullion to trade slowly, PGMs stable.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bullion to trade slowly, PGMs stable.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - June 16 -------------
Bullion markets are expected to trade quietly, with gold and silver perhaps drifting lower to test $340.00 and $4.68 per ounce respectively, analysts said on Monday.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were likely to see more stable trading conditions and remain steady on Russian supply scarcity, they said.
GOLD -
The precious metals sector is expected to trade fairly slowly, with many participants attending a major conference in Prague, traders said.
There was also the EU summit in Amsterdam and an upcoming G-7 meeting, although these were unlikely to have much influence on bullion.
"It is very quiet, and there is absolutely little movement," one European trader said.
Gold prices were expected to drift back towards the $340 level, with further support expected around $337.50.
At 0824 GMT spot gold was quoted at $340.70/341.00, little changed from Friday's close.
SILVER -
Little movement was seen likely, with prices straddling the $4.70 level in quiet trade.
But if the market veered lower there might be a test of important support.
"It has to hold the $4.68 level," the European trader said.
At 0824 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.70/4.71, also little different.
PLATINUM -
The market was holding comfortably around the $430 level, but activity in this metal and palladium was likely to prove less intense this week with lease rates slightly softer.

News that officials from the U.S.-based hedge fund Tiger Management visited Japan last week with a view to selling palladium had little noticeable impact on that market, which was unmoved at $202/207 an ounce.
Platinum was indicated at $430.00/435.00, against a previous close of $431.00/432.00.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
